record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: Prove the algebraic version of Birkhoff conjecture for outer billiards in a non-Euclidean surface of constant curvature. The next problem is a generalization of the previous one.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.4. Prove the algebraic version of Birkhoff conjecture for outer billiards in a non-Euclidean surface of constant curvature. The next problem is a generalization of the previous one.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a complete simply connected two-dimensional Riemannian surface of constant curvature $K
eq 0$ — i.e. either the round sphere $S^2$ (when $K>0$) or the hyperbolic plane $H^2$ (when $K<0$). Let $\gamma\subset M$ be a smooth, strictly geodesically convex, closed curve bounding a domain $D$ whose complement contains no pair of points joined by a unique geodesic ambiguity (so that the outer billiard map is well-defined on an open subset of $M\setminus\overline{D}$).

The outer (dual) billiard map $T_\gamma$ associated with $\gamma$ is defined as follows. For a point $p$ in a suitable neighborhood of $\gamma$ in $M\setminus\overline{D}$, let $\ell_p$ be the (oriented) geodesic from $p$ that is tangent to $\gamma$ at a point $q(p)$, chosen by a fixed orientation convention. Then $T_\gamma(p)$ is the point on $\ell_p$ such that $q(p)$ is the geodesic midpoint of the segment from $p$ to $T_\gamma(p)$.

The outer billiard $T_\gamma$ is said to be polynomially integrable (algebraically integrable) if there exists a non-constant function $F:U	o\mathbb{R}$, defined on an invariant open neighborhood $U$ of $\gamma$, such that:
(i) $F\circ T_\gamma = F$ on $U$;
(ii) in any (and hence every) standard embedding of $M$ as a quadric in $\mathbb{R}^3$ (the sphere $\{x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2=1/K\}$ for $K>0$, or the upper sheet of the hyperboloid $\{x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=1/K\}$ for $K<0$), the function $F$ is the restriction to $U$ of a polynomial in the ambient coordinates $(x_1,x_2,x_3)$.

Problem. Prove that if the outer billiard $T_\gamma$ associated with a closed strictly geodesically convex smooth curve $\gamma$ on $M$ is polynomially integrable in the above sense, then $\gamma$ is a conic in $M$, i.e. the intersection of the quadric model of $M$ with an affine quadric in $\mathbb{R}^3$ (equivalently, a geodesic circle, an ellipse, or another classical conic of constant curvature geometry).
artifact.status_search_result: The corresponding algebraic Birkhoff conjecture for inner (Birkhoff) billiards on surfaces of constant curvature has been established by Bialy–Mironov and Glutsyuk. The algebraic version of the Birkhoff conjecture for outer billiards is known in the affine (flat) plane (Tabachnikov), but for outer billiards on the sphere and hyperbolic plane it appears to remain open; the listed problem and recent work on "Integrable outer billiards and rigidity" continue to address it without a full resolution.

status_evidence.title: On polynomially integrable Birkhoff billiards on surfaces of constant curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Resolves the algebraic Birkhoff conjecture for inner billiards on sphere and hyperbolic plane.
status_evidence.claim: Inner-billiard analogue solved on constant curvature surfaces.

status_evidence.title: Integrable Outer billiards and rigidity
status_evidence.snippet: Recent investigations of integrable outer billiards, indicating outer case is still under active study.
status_evidence.claim: Outer-billiard algebraic Birkhoff conjecture on non-Euclidean constant curvature surfaces remains an active open problem.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic Birkhoff conjecture for billiards on Sphere and Hyperbolic plane
status_evidence.snippet: Studies obstructions to polynomial integrability for billiards on sphere and hyperbolic plane, building on Tabachnikov's outer billiard method.
status_evidence.claim: Related obstruction results known but outer-billiard rigidity not fully established in non-Euclidean setting.
